chunks: From him, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from Abdullah ibn Nahik, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darradj, from a group of our companions, from the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:

"The absent one is judged against when evidence is established against him, and his property is sold, and his debt is paid on his behalf while he is absent, and the absent one remains upon his proof when he returns."
He said, "And the money is not given to the one who established the evidence except with guarantors."

key_terms.الْغَائِبُ: The absent person (one who is away and whose status/location is known but not present)
key_terms.حُجَّتُهُ: His proof / evidence (his right to claim his property)
key_terms.يُقْضَى عَلَيْهِ: He is judged against / executed against (his assets are used to settle claims)
key_terms.يُقْضَى عَنْهُ دَيْنُهُ: His debt is paid on his behalf

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling regarding the property and debts of an absent person?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the judicial management of an absent person's (*gha'ib*) estate, emphasizing that while his assets are liquidated to settle debts upon sufficient evidence, he retains full ownership rights upon his return. A key scholarly nuance is the requirement of sureties (*kufala*) for the claimant to receive the proceeds, ensuring the absent owner is protected against misappropriation or loss during his absence. This mechanism reflects the Shia juristic balance between preserving the creditor's rights and safeguarding the property of the missing individual.
